summary: StorageFacade is the main user entry point: it builds and owns a connection from a storage profile and auth profile, resolves a backend from the registry, and dispatches read/write/enumerate/delete/metadata/copy/directory calls after checking the backend implements the matching protocol (UnsupportedOperationError otherwise). It enforces LocationPolicy confinement on every path, applies stream-transform pipelines, and offers sequential, random (RangedReadProtocol) and buffered read modes. The package re-exports StorageFacade and copy_between.
key_classes: StorageFacade — protocol-checked dispatch to a registered backend with owned connection, location policy and transform pipelines
key_functions: StorageFacade(provider_type, storage_profile=None, *, auth_profile=None, oauth_provider=None, token_store=None, policy=None) — creates connection and backend; closes on construction failure
StorageFacade.from_path(path, storage_profile=None, *, auth_profile=None, oauth_provider=None, token_store=None, policy=None) — infers provider from the path scheme
StorageFacade.supports(protocol) -> bool — isinstance check against a runtime_checkable protocol
StorageFacade.read(path, *, pipeline=None, infer=False, gpg=None, gzip=None) -> bytes
StorageFacade.read_stream(path, *, pipeline=None, infer=False, gpg=None, gzip=None, access='sequential'|'random'|'buffered', range_policy=None) -> BinaryIO
StorageFacade.write(path, data, *, pipeline=None, create_parents=True) / write_stream(path, stream, *, pipeline=None, create_parents=True)
StorageFacade.close() / context manager — terminal close of the owned connection
extension_points: Any backend registered with @register_storage_backend becomes usable through the facade; operations light up according to the storage protocols the backend satisfies.
Transforms plug in via Pipeline/StreamTransform arguments; read-side suffix inference via infer=True.
LocationPolicy (policy=) and profile ROOT_PATH constrain reachable paths; RangePolicy tunes random reads.
lifecycle_notes: The facade owns the connection it creates; close() is terminal and idempotent; later I/O raises StorageConnectionError while supports() stays available.
Returned sequential/random streams are caller-owned and should be closed before the facade; buffered results are independent.
Construction connects immediately (create_connection + connect); cleanup errors during failed construction are attached as exception notes.
HTTP without a profile instantiates HTTPStorageProfile, which requires the [http] extra; local use needs only the base install.
A LOCAL profile with ROOT_PATH and CREATE_PATH creates that directory at construction time.
Random access on LOCAL returns the native seekable handle instead of going through RangedReadProtocol.
documentation_hooks: Getting started / quick start: from_path, context manager, read/write.
Capability model: supports(), UnsupportedOperationError, mapping of facade methods to storage protocols and the backend support matrix.
Read access modes (sequential/random/buffered) and RangePolicy precedence.
Transforms on read/write and suffix inference.
Location policy and path confinement for local and remote providers.

risks: from_path docstring documents parameters named `profile` and `auth`, but the signature uses storage_profile and auth_profile, and policy is undocumented.
supports() and _require use isinstance on runtime_checkable protocols, which checks method presence only, not signatures (e.g. local mkdir's positional `parents`).
Facade list_objects defaults delimiter='/' while backend/protocol list_objects default to None (recursive); documented in README.md but easy to miss.
write(create_parents=False) semantics differ by backend: Local/SFTP enforce it, S3/HTTP ignore it.
